tasks.title: Bootstrap Worker foundation: bindings, middleware chain, error envelope, health endpoint, test harness
tasks.description: Turn the hello-world Hono starter into the platform skeleton: configure all Cloudflare bindings in wrangler.jsonc, build the shared middleware chain (request id, structured logging, CORS), define the JSON success/error envelope, add /v1/health, export fetch + scheduled handlers, and wire the vitest Workers test harness.
tasks.details:
Existing state: src/index.ts is a bare `new Hono()` app; wrangler.jsonc has no bindings. Steps:
1. Add deps: `zod` (runtime), `vitest` + `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` (dev). Add `"test": "vitest run"` to package.json scripts (CLAUDE.md already references `npm test`).
2. wrangler.jsonc: add `d1_databases` (binding `DB`, database_name `faceless-api`), two `kv_namespaces` (`CACHE`, `RATE`) with placeholder ids for local dev, `assets: { directory: "public" }`, and `triggers: { crons: ["0 5 * * *"] }` (daily; per-source cadence refined in task 3). Run `npm run cf-typegen` to regenerate `CloudflareBindings`.
3. Restructure src/index.ts: `const app = new Hono<{ Bindings: CloudflareBindings, Variables: { requestId: string, keyCtx?: KeyContext } }>()`. Middleware order: requestId → structured JSON logger (log `{requestId, route, method, status, latencyMs, keyId?, creditsCharged?}` via console.log JSON) → CORS. Export `default { fetch: app.fetch, scheduled }` with a stub `scheduled` handler (filled in task 3).
4. Envelope in src/lib/envelope.ts: success `{ ok: true, data, meta? }`; error `{ ok: false, error: { code, message, docs_url } }` — machine-parsable code + human hint + docs URL per PRD. Register `app.onError` + `app.notFound` to always emit the error envelope; map HTTPException status codes to stable codes (`unauthorized`, `not_found`, `rate_limited`, `payment_required`, `internal`).
5. `GET /v1/health` in src/routes/health.ts returning `{ status: "ok", version }` (no auth — UptimeRobot target).
6. vitest.config.ts using `defineWorkersConfig` from @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers with `wrangler: { configPath: "./wrangler.jsonc" }` so tests get real KV/D1 bindings via miniflare.
Use named exports and explicit return types throughout (house rules).
tasks.testStrategy: Worker-level integration tests via vitest-pool-workers using `SELF.fetch`: /v1/health returns 200 with `{status:"ok"}`; unknown route returns 404 with the exact error-envelope shape; thrown HTTPException produces envelope with correct code and docs_url; response includes request id header. `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, and `npm run build` (dry-run deploy) all pass, proving bindings config is valid.

subtasks.title: Add zod, vitest, and @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers dependencies plus npm test script
subtasks.description: Install the runtime and dev dependencies required by the foundation work and wire the `npm test` script that CLAUDE.md already references, leaving the repo's quality gates green.
subtasks.details: Run `npm install zod` (runtime dependency) and `npm install -D vitest @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` — pick versions compatible with the repo's wrangler 4.x (vitest-pool-workers pins a supported vitest range; check its peerDependencies and align vitest accordingly rather than blindly taking latest). Add `"test": "vitest run"` to package.json scripts. Do not create vitest.config.ts yet (that is subtask 5); `npm test` may fail with 'no test files' at this point, which is acceptable. Verify package-lock.json is updated and that `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, and `npm run build` all still pass. Note: these deps are named in the parent task, so no separate ask-first approval is needed despite the new-dependency house rule.
subtasks.testStrategy: `npm ls zod vitest @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` resolves without peer-dependency errors; `node -e "require('zod')"` equivalent import compiles under typecheck; lint/typecheck/build all exit 0.

subtasks.title: Configure wrangler.jsonc bindings (D1, KV, assets, cron) and regenerate CloudflareBindings via cf-typegen
subtasks.description: Author all Cloudflare bindings from scratch in wrangler.jsonc — everything is currently commented out — then regenerate the CloudflareBindings type so downstream code can type the Hono app against real bindings.
subtasks.details: In wrangler.jsonc add: `d1_databases` with `{ binding: "DB", database_name: "faceless-api", database_id: "<placeholder>" }`; two `kv_namespaces` entries `{ binding: "CACHE", id: "<placeholder>" }` and `{ binding: "RATE", id: "<placeholder>" }` (placeholder ids are fine for local dev/miniflare); `assets: { directory: "public" }` (create an empty `public/` directory with a minimal placeholder index.html so the assets directory exists); and `triggers: { crons: ["0 5 * * *"] }` for the daily refresh (per-source cadence is refined in task 3 of the parent plan). Then run `npm run cf-typegen` to regenerate the CloudflareBindings interface (worker-configuration.d.ts) and confirm it now declares DB (D1Database), CACHE and RATE (KVNamespace). Keep JSONC comments explaining each binding's purpose. Finish with lint/typecheck/build green — `npm run build` (dry-run deploy) is the real validator that wrangler accepts the config.
subtasks.testStrategy: `npm run build` (wrangler dry-run deploy) succeeds, proving the config parses and bindings are well-formed; generated worker-configuration.d.ts contains DB/CACHE/RATE with correct types; `npm run dev` boots without binding errors.

subtasks.title: Restructure src/index.ts: typed Hono app, requestId → JSON logger → CORS middleware, fetch + scheduled exports
subtasks.description: Replace the 9-line hello-world app with the platform skeleton: a Hono app typed against CloudflareBindings and shared Variables, the ordered middleware chain, and a default export exposing both fetch and a stub scheduled handler.
subtasks.details: Rewrite src/index.ts as `const app = new Hono<{ Bindings: CloudflareBindings; Variables: { requestId: string; keyCtx?: KeyContext } }>()` (declare a minimal `KeyContext` placeholder type, e.g. in src/lib/types.ts, to be fleshed out by the auth task). Middleware in this exact order: (1) requestId — generate via crypto.randomUUID(), set on `c.set('requestId', ...)` and echo as a response header (e.g. `x-request-id`); (2) structured JSON logger — after `await next()`, `console.log(JSON.stringify({ requestId, route, method, status, latencyMs, keyId?, creditsCharged? }))` measuring latency around next(); (3) CORS via hono/cors. Export `default { fetch: app.fetch, scheduled }` where `scheduled` is a stub `(controller: ScheduledController, env: CloudflareBindings, ctx: ExecutionContext): Promise<void>` that just logs — task 3 of the parent plan fills it in. Also export the `app` instance as a named export so routes/tests can reference it. Use named exports and explicit return types per house rules; keep a temporary root route or none at all (404 handling arrives in subtask 4).
subtasks.testStrategy: `npm run typecheck` proves the Bindings/Variables generics resolve against the generated CloudflareBindings; `npm run dev` boots and any request logs one JSON line containing requestId/method/status/latencyMs and returns the x-request-id header; formal SELF.fetch assertions land in subtask 5.

subtasks.title: Implement envelope (src/lib/envelope.ts), onError/notFound handlers, and GET /v1/health route
subtasks.description: Define the machine-parsable JSON success/error envelope used by every endpoint, register global error and 404 handlers that always emit it with stable error codes, and add the unauthenticated /v1/health route for uptime monitoring.
subtasks.details: src/lib/envelope.ts: named helpers with explicit return types — `ok<T>(data: T, meta?: ...)` producing `{ ok: true, data, meta? }` and `err(code, message, docsUrl)` producing `{ ok: false, error: { code, message, docs_url } }`. Define the stable code union: `unauthorized` (401), `not_found` (404), `rate_limited` (429), `payment_required` (402), `internal` (500), with a status→code mapping function for HTTPException instances. In src/index.ts register `app.onError` (map HTTPException status via the table, anything else → 500 `internal`; never leak stack traces; include a docs_url pointing at a stable anchor like `https://<domain>/docs#errors`) and `app.notFound` (404 envelope with code `not_found`). src/routes/health.ts: a named-export Hono sub-router with `GET /` returning `ok({ status: 'ok', version })` — version from package.json import or a build-time constant — mounted at `/v1/health` in index.ts with no auth (UptimeRobot target). Lint/typecheck/build green.
subtasks.testStrategy: Manual smoke via `npm run dev`: GET /v1/health → 200 `{ok:true,data:{status:'ok',...}}`; GET /nope → 404 with exact error-envelope shape and code `not_found`; a temporary route throwing HTTPException(401) yields the `unauthorized` envelope with docs_url. Automated SELF.fetch coverage is subtask 5.

subtasks.title: Create vitest.config.ts with defineWorkersConfig and write SELF.fetch integration tests
subtasks.description: Wire the Workers test harness so tests run inside miniflare with the real KV/D1 bindings from wrangler.jsonc, then cover the foundation's contract: health 200, 404 envelope, HTTPException envelope, and request-id header.
subtasks.details: Create vitest.config.ts using `defineWorkersConfig` from `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers/config` with `test.poolOptions.workers.wrangler.configPath: './wrangler.jsonc'` so miniflare provisions DB/CACHE/RATE from the real config. Add the pool-workers types (`@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` types entry or a test tsconfig) so `cloudflare:test` imports typecheck. Write test/index.spec.ts using `import { SELF } from 'cloudflare:test'`: (1) GET /v1/health → 200 with `{ok:true, data:{status:'ok'}}`; (2) unknown route → 404 with the exact error-envelope shape `{ok:false, error:{code:'not_found', message, docs_url}}`; (3) a route that throws HTTPException produces the envelope with the mapped stable code and docs_url — either hit a deliberate test-only route or import the app and register a throwing route in the test; (4) every response carries the x-request-id header (non-empty, unique per request). This is the notoriously fiddly step: if `npm test` fails on version alignment between wrangler 4.x, vitest, and the pool, resolve by pinning the versions the pool's peerDependencies demand (adjusting subtask 1's installs). Finish with `npm test`, lint, typecheck, and build all green.
subtasks.testStrategy: `npm test` runs the Workers pool and all four integration tests pass deterministically (run twice to confirm no flake); tests fail meaningfully if the envelope shape or header is changed (mutate one field locally to confirm, then revert); CI-parity check: lint + typecheck + test + build all exit 0 in sequence.

tasks.expansionPrompt: Break into subtasks along the five independent workstreams: (1) add zod + vitest + @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers deps and the npm test script; (2) configure wrangler.jsonc bindings (D1 `DB`, KV `CACHE`/`RATE`, assets dir `public/`, cron trigger) and run cf-typegen to regenerate CloudflareBindings — note wrangler.jsonc currently has ALL bindings commented out, so this is from scratch; (3) restructure src/index.ts from the 9-line hello-world app to typed Hono<{Bindings, Variables}> with requestId → structured JSON logger → CORS middleware and `export default { fetch, scheduled }` with a stub scheduled handler; (4) implement src/lib/envelope.ts success/error envelope plus app.onError/app.notFound mapping HTTPException statuses to stable codes, and GET /v1/health in src/routes/health.ts; (5) create vitest.config.ts with defineWorkersConfig pointing at wrangler.jsonc and write the SELF.fetch integration tests (health 200, 404 envelope, HTTPException envelope, request-id header). Each subtask should end with lint/typecheck/build green.

tasks.title: DataSource interface, source registry, and generic /v1/data/:source query endpoint
tasks.description: Build the niche-agnostic heart: a DataSource TypeScript interface (slug, zod record schema, fetchFresh, refresh policy, declared query capabilities), a registry mapping slugs to sources, and a generic /v1/data/:source endpoint with pagination and source-declared filters — so adding a source file + registry entry is the whole cost of a new dataset.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests: registry lookup, unknown slug → 404 envelope, pagination math (page/per_page bounds, total counts), filter application against a fixture demo source, invalid query param → 400 envelope with zod issue detail. Integration test via SELF.fetch exercising /v1/data/:source end-to-end with the demo source. Assert no source-specific branches exist in routes (code review checklist item).

subtasks.title: Define the DataSource<T> interface and shared source types in src/sources/types.ts
subtasks.description: Create the niche-agnostic DataSource TypeScript contract — slug, title, zod recordSchema, fetchFresh, refresh policy, queryParams, optional creditCost — with generics designed so a heterogeneous registry stays type-safe.
subtasks.details: In src/sources/types.ts define `export interface DataSource<T extends z.ZodTypeAny = z.ZodTypeAny>` with: `slug: string` (e.g. 'uk-planning'), `title: string`, `recordSchema: T` (zod schema of one normalized record), `fetchFresh(env: CloudflareBindings): Promise<z.infer<T>[]>`, `refresh: { cron: string; cacheTtlSeconds: number }`, `queryParams: z.ZodObject<any>` (per-request-validated filters this source declares), and `creditCost?: number` (default 1, consumed later by task 7). Get the generics right: registry entries must be storable as `DataSource` (erased/default type param) while individual source modules keep full inference from their own recordSchema — add a type-level test or helper (e.g. `defineSource`) if needed to prove both directions compile. Also export any shared helper types the route/filter layer will need (e.g. `SourceRecord<S> = z.infer<S['recordSchema']>`). Explicit return types on all exported functions, no `any` leaking into the public surface beyond the documented `z.ZodObject<any>` for queryParams. Nothing dataset-specific may appear here (CLAUDE.md isolation rule).
subtasks.testStrategy: Type-level assertions (expectTypeOf via vitest or tsd-style compile checks): a concrete source with a specific zod schema assigns to `DataSource`; `z.infer` of recordSchema flows through fetchFresh's return type; a mistyped fetchFresh return fails compilation. `npm run typecheck` passes with strict mode.

subtasks.title: Build the source registry with getSource lookup and an in-memory demo source
subtasks.description: Create src/sources/registry.ts mapping slugs to DataSource entries with a getSource(slug) helper, plus a demo in-memory source with fixture records so the endpoint and tests work before task 3's real sources/cache land.
subtasks.details: src/sources/registry.ts: `export const registry: Record<string, DataSource>` and `export function getSource(slug: string): DataSource | undefined` (explicit return type; named exports per conventions). Create src/sources/demo.ts: an in-memory demo source with a small zod recordSchema covering the filterable types the generic filter engine must handle (at least one string field for substring matching, one enum/literal or number field for equality matching, and a date-ish string), `fetchFresh` returning ~10–20 deterministic fixture records synchronously wrapped in a Promise, a `queryParams` z.object declaring 2–3 filters, and a refresh policy with placeholder cron/TTL values. Register it in the registry. Keep the demo source clearly marked as test scaffolding to be joined (not replaced) by real sources in task 3. All dataset-specific content lives only in src/sources/demo.ts plus its registry entry — nothing elsewhere.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests: getSource('demo') returns the source and getSource('nope') returns undefined; demo fixture records all parse against the demo recordSchema; queryParams schema accepts declared filters and rejects unknown-typed values.

subtasks.title: Implement GET /v1/data/:source with generic schema-driven filtering and pagination (extract src/sources/query.ts)
subtasks.description: Build the generic query endpoint: 404 envelope for unknown slugs, query validation via source.queryParams extended with page/per_page coercion, a reusable filter/paginate core in src/sources/query.ts driven purely by the zod param shape, and the response envelope with meta.
subtasks.details: src/sources/query.ts (extracted so tasks 9 and 10 — MCP tools and x402 routes — can reuse it without going through Hono): (a) `buildQuerySchema(source)` returning `source.queryParams.extend({ page: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).default(1), per_page: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(100).default(25) })`; (b) `applyFilters(records, params, queryParams)` that introspects the zod shape of each declared param and applies equality for numbers/booleans/enums and case-insensitive substring for strings — no per-dataset branches anywhere (any dataset-specific conditional is a design bug per CLAUDE.md); (c) `paginate(records, page, per_page)` returning `{ items, total }`. src/routes/data.ts: `GET /v1/data/:source` — unknown slug → 404 using task 1's error envelope; validate the query string against the built schema, zod failure → 400 envelope with issue detail; obtain records via the cache layer abstraction (until task 3 lands, call `source.fetchFresh(env)` behind a thin `getRecords(env, source)` seam so task 3 swaps in KV caching without touching this route); apply filters, paginate, respond with success envelope `meta: { page, per_page, total, source: slug, last_refreshed_at }` (last_refreshed_at may be the fetch time until refresh_log exists). Mount the route in src/index.ts.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests against the demo source fixtures: applyFilters equality and substring behavior per param type, combined filters, pagination math (bounds, total counts, out-of-range page returns empty items with correct total), per_page clamped at 100. Route-level: unknown slug → 404 envelope; invalid param (e.g. page=0, non-numeric per_page) → 400 envelope with zod issue detail.

subtasks.title: Add the sources-listing endpoint and full unit + SELF.fetch integration test suite
subtasks.description: Expose registry metadata via GET /v1/sources (title, slug, freshness, supported params — the future feed for MCP list_sources), and write the end-to-end vitest-pool-workers tests covering the whole task including the invalid-param 400 envelope.
subtasks.details: In src/routes/data.ts add `GET /v1/sources` (also decide whether bare `GET /v1/data` aliases it or 404s — document the choice): iterate the registry and return, per source, `{ slug, title, refresh: { cron, cacheTtlSeconds }, last_refreshed_at, params }` where `params` is derived generically from each source's queryParams zod shape (param name + inferred type + optionality) — this listing later feeds MCP list_sources in task 9, so keep the shape stable and serializable. Wrap in the standard success envelope. Then complete the task's test suite using task 1's vitest Workers harness: SELF.fetch integration tests for `/v1/data/demo` happy path (envelope shape, meta fields, records validate against demo recordSchema), filtered query, paginated query, unknown slug 404 envelope, invalid query param 400 envelope with zod issue detail, and `/v1/sources` listing containing the demo entry with its declared params. Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, and `npm test` clean.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration via SELF.fetch (vitest-pool-workers): GET /v1/sources returns 200 with the demo source's slug/title/params; GET /v1/data/demo end-to-end with pagination and filter params matches unit-level expectations; invalid param → 400 envelope; unknown slug → 404 envelope. Full quality gates (lint, typecheck, test) pass.

tasks.expansionPrompt: Split into: (1) define the DataSource<T extends z.ZodTypeAny> interface in src/sources/types.ts (slug, title, recordSchema, fetchFresh, refresh policy, queryParams, creditCost) — get the generics right so registry entries stay heterogeneous but type-safe; (2) build src/sources/registry.ts with getSource(slug) plus an in-memory demo source with fixture records for tests; (3) implement GET /v1/data/:source in src/routes/data.ts — unknown-slug 404 envelope, queryParams extended with page/per_page coercion, generic filter application driven purely by the zod param shape (equality/substring by type — no per-dataset branches), pagination, and envelope meta {page, per_page, total, source, last_refreshed_at}; (4) implement the sources-listing endpoint (GET /v1/data or /v1/sources) exposing registry metadata, and write the unit + SELF.fetch integration tests including the invalid-param 400 envelope. Extract the query/filter core so tasks 9 and 10 can reuse it (src/sources/query.ts).

tasks.title: uk-planning seed source with Blind Mode schema, KV caching, and cron refresh pipeline
tasks.description: Implement the first real DataSource pulling UK planning applications from the official planning.data.gov.uk JSON API with personal-data fields excluded at the schema level (Blind Mode), plus the shared infrastructure it exercises: KV response caching, the scheduled-handler refresh loop writing refresh_log to D1, freshness metadata, and fixture fallback for offline dev.
tasks.details:
1. Start the D1 migrations workflow now (Phase 1 needs refresh_log): create `migrations/0001_refresh_log.sql` — `refresh_log(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, source_slug TEXT, status TEXT, records INTEGER, duration_ms INTEGER, created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')))`; document `wrangler d1 migrations create/apply` usage (local apply is free; production apply is an ask-first op per CLAUDE.md).
2. src/sources/uk-planning.ts: recordSchema with reference, authority, status, decision, dates (received/validated/decided), site-level location (postcode/point), description — NO applicant name/agent/contact fields; strip unknown keys with `.strip()` so personal data is dropped at ingest and never stored (UK GDPR Blind Mode). fetchFresh() calls planning.data.gov.uk's dataset API (e.g. `https://www.planning.data.gov.uk/entity.json?dataset=planning-application&limit=...` with pagination loop), maps entities → normalized records, and validates each through the schema. On fetch failure in local dev, fall back to `src/sources/fixtures/uk-planning.json` (PRD: offline-capable dev). queryParams: authority, status, decided_after/decided_before, q (description substring). refresh: daily cron, cacheTtlSeconds 86400.
3. src/sources/cache.ts (generic, source-agnostic): `readCached(env, source)` → KV `data:<slug>` (records + `last_refreshed_at`), on miss run fetchFresh and populate; `refreshSource(env, source)` → fetchFresh, write KV, insert refresh_log row (status ok/error, record count, duration). Wire the `scheduled` handler from task 1: iterate registry, refresh sources matching the cron event, never throw (log failures to refresh_log so the operator sees them).
4. Wire /v1/data/:source (task 2) to read through this cache and expose `last_refreshed_at` in meta.
Verify current planning.data.gov.uk endpoint paths/params at implementation time — record the exact URL used in the source file header comment.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit: schema rejects/strips personal-data fields (feed a fixture containing applicant_name and assert it never appears in output); origin-response → normalized-record mapping against recorded fixtures; fixture fallback path when fetch rejects. Integration (pool-workers): trigger the scheduled handler via `SELF.scheduled` / runDurableObjectAlarm-style test API, assert KV populated and refresh_log row written (query D1 binding in test); /v1/data/uk-planning serves cached data with last_refreshed_at and filters by authority/status. Mock origin with fetchMock so tests never hit the network.

subtasks.title: Bootstrap D1 migrations workflow with migrations/0001_refresh_log.sql
subtasks.description: Establish the D1 migrations pattern for the repo (no migrations/ directory exists yet) by creating the first migration for the refresh_log table and documenting the local vs production apply workflow.
subtasks.details: Create `migrations/0001_refresh_log.sql` containing: `CREATE TABLE refresh_log (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, source_slug TEXT, status TEXT, records INTEGER, duration_ms INTEGER, created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')));`. Ensure `wrangler.jsonc` has the D1 binding configured with `migrations_dir` pointing at `migrations/` (add if missing) and run `npm run cf-typegen` if bindings change. Document the workflow in `docs/` (or a README section): `wrangler d1 migrations create <db> <name>` to scaffold, `wrangler d1 migrations apply <db> --local` for free local apply during dev, and note that `wrangler d1 migrations apply <db> --remote` against production is an ask-first operation per CLAUDE.md. Verify the migration applies cleanly locally and the table shape matches what src/sources/cache.ts will insert (source_slug, status, records, duration_ms).
subtasks.testStrategy: Run `wrangler d1 migrations apply <db> --local` and confirm success; query the local D1 with `wrangler d1 execute --local --command "PRAGMA table_info(refresh_log)"` to assert columns and default. Pool-workers tests in later subtasks will exercise the table via real inserts.

subtasks.title: uk-planning recordSchema with Blind Mode and source-declared queryParams
subtasks.description: Create src/sources/uk-planning.ts with a zod recordSchema that structurally excludes personal data (Blind Mode) — only site-level fields, unknown keys stripped — plus the queryParams schema declaring the filters this source supports.
subtasks.details: In `src/sources/uk-planning.ts`, define `recordSchema` as a zod object with: reference, authority, status, decision, dates (received/validated/decided), site-level location only (postcode, point/coordinates), and description. Explicitly NO applicant name, agent, or contact fields — and apply `.strip()` so any unknown keys from the origin are dropped at parse time, meaning personal data is never stored (UK GDPR Blind Mode; this is compliance-critical, not just hygiene). Add a comment on the schema stating the Blind Mode invariant so future edits don't reintroduce personal fields. Define `queryParams` as a zod object with: authority, status, decided_after/decided_before (date strings), and q (description substring match). Stub the DataSource object conforming to the task-2 interface (slug 'uk-planning', title, recordSchema, queryParams, refresh: { cron for daily, cacheTtlSeconds: 86400 }) with fetchFresh left as a placeholder for subtask 3, and add the registry entry per the dataset-isolation rule (source file + registry entry only).
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests: feed a record containing applicant_name, agent_email, and other personal keys through recordSchema.parse and assert those keys never appear in the output; assert required site-level fields survive; assert queryParams accepts valid filters and rejects malformed dates with zod issues.

subtasks.title: fetchFresh() against planning.data.gov.uk with pagination, mapping, and fixture fallback
subtasks.description: Implement fetchFresh() calling the live planning.data.gov.uk entity.json API with a pagination loop, mapping raw entities to normalized records validated through the Blind Mode schema, with fallback to a local fixture when the fetch fails in local dev.
subtasks.details: Verify the current planning.data.gov.uk endpoint shape at implementation time (expected form: `https://www.planning.data.gov.uk/entity.json?dataset=planning-application&limit=...` — confirm dataset slug, pagination params, and response envelope against the live API) and record the exact URL and verification date in a header comment in `src/sources/uk-planning.ts`. Implement the pagination loop (offset/cursor per the API's actual scheme, bounded page size, sane upper limit), map each entity to the normalized record shape, and validate every record through recordSchema.parse so stripping happens at ingest. On fetch failure (network error or non-2xx) in local dev, fall back to `src/sources/fixtures/uk-planning.json` — create that fixture from a real recorded API response (with personal fields present in the raw capture so tests can prove they get stripped). Surface fetch errors to the caller in production paths so refreshSource can log status 'error'.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests with fetchMock (no live network): mock a two-page entity.json response and assert the pagination loop aggregates all records; assert entity→record mapping against the recorded fixture (snapshot or field-level asserts); reject the mocked fetch and assert the fixture fallback path returns parsed, Blind-Mode-stripped records.

subtasks.title: Generic src/sources/cache.ts (KV read-through + refreshSource) and scheduled-handler wiring
subtasks.description: Build the source-agnostic cache layer: readCached() KV read-through and refreshSource() writing KV plus a refresh_log row to D1, then wire the task-1 scheduled handler to iterate the registry and refresh matching sources without ever throwing.
subtasks.details: Create `src/sources/cache.ts` — generic over any DataSource, no uk-planning-specific logic (dataset isolation rule). `readCached(env, source)`: read KV key `data:<slug>` holding `{ records, last_refreshed_at }`; on miss, call source.fetchFresh(), write the KV entry (respecting source.refresh.cacheTtlSeconds), and return it. `refreshSource(env, source)`: time the fetchFresh() call, write the KV entry on success, and insert a refresh_log row into D1 either way — status 'ok' with record count and duration_ms, or status 'error' with the failure captured — so the operator sees failures in refresh_log rather than silent drops. Wire the `scheduled` handler exported from src/index.ts (task 1) to iterate the source registry, select sources whose refresh.cron matches the triggering cron event, and call refreshSource for each inside a try/catch per source — the handler must never throw, and one failing source must not block others.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests: readCached hit returns KV data without calling fetchFresh (spy); miss populates KV. refreshSource success writes KV + 'ok' row; a rejecting fetchFresh writes an 'error' row and does not clobber existing KV data. Scheduled-handler test: registry with one healthy and one throwing source — handler resolves without throwing and both outcomes appear in refresh_log.

subtasks.title: Wire /v1/data/:source through the cache with last_refreshed_at, plus unit and pool-workers integration tests

tasks.title: OpenAPI 3.1 spec at /openapi.json generated from the zod schemas
tasks.description: Make the zod schemas the single source of truth by auto-generating an OpenAPI 3.1 document served at /openapi.json, covering every /v1 route with per-source paths derived from the registry — the same spec later feeds the Scalar docs embed and validates the MCP tool surface.
tasks.details:
Preferred approach: `@hono/zod-openapi` (Hono's official zod-to-OpenAPI integration, supports OpenAPI 3.1 via `app.doc31`/`getOpenAPI31Document`) — define routes with `createRoute({ method, path, request: { params, query }, responses })` and mount on an `OpenAPIHono` app. Alternative if migrating existing routes is too invasive: keep plain Hono routes and build the document with `@asteasolutions/zod-to-openapi`'s OpenApiGeneratorV31, registering each registry entry programmatically. Either way (ask before adding the dependency per CLAUDE.md; it's PRD-mandated so flag not block):
1. For each registry source, generate `GET /v1/data/{slug}` path items with query parameters from `source.queryParams` + pagination params, and response schema `envelope(array(recordSchema))` — iterate the registry at spec-build time so new sources appear automatically.
2. Document /v1/health, /v1/usage, /v1/keys, /v1/waitlist as they land (later tasks extend the same generator — keep a `registerRoute` helper so each task adds its own spec entry).
3. Add bearer/api-key securityScheme (`Authorization: Bearer <key>`), error-envelope component schema, and X-Credits-Remaining response-header documentation.
4. Serve at `GET /openapi.json` with long cache headers; include `info.version` from package.json, server URL from env (placeholder domain until purchased).
Note zod v4 also offers native `z.toJSONSchema()` — use it only if the chosen integration lags zod v4 support; pin whatever combination works and record why.
tasks.testStrategy: Integration test fetches /openapi.json and asserts: valid JSON, `openapi: "3.1.x"`, a path exists for every registry slug (add a source in test → path appears), query params in the spec match the source's queryParams shape, and the security scheme is present. Validate the document in CI with a spec validator (e.g. `@seriousme/openapi-schema-validator` in a unit test) to catch generation regressions.

subtasks.title: Evaluate and pin the zod-to-OpenAPI generation approach

subtasks.details: Check the installed zod version in package.json first, since the zod v4 vs openapi-library compatibility churn is the main risk. For @hono/zod-openapi: confirm it supports OpenAPI 3.1 output via app.doc31/getOpenAPI31Document and works with the project's zod version; assess how invasive migrating existing /v1 route definitions to OpenAPIHono would be. For @asteasolutions/zod-to-openapi: confirm OpenApiGeneratorV31 compatibility and that plain Hono routes can stay untouched. Fall back to zod v4 native z.toJSONSchema only if both integrations lag zod v4 support. Pin exact versions of whatever combination works. Record the decision, the version-compatibility rationale, and any known caveats in a short ADR-style note (e.g. docs/decisions or a comment block near the generator module). The dependency is PRD-mandated, so per CLAUDE.md flag it to the user rather than silently adding it — surface the choice and proceed once acknowledged.
subtasks.testStrategy: No automated tests for this subtask; acceptance is a recorded decision note with pinned versions, plus `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` passing after the dependency is added, proving the chosen library resolves and bundles cleanly on Workers.

subtasks.title: Implement registry-driven path generation with a registerRoute helper
subtasks.description: Build the spec generator that iterates the DataSource registry at spec-build time, emitting a GET /v1/data/{slug} path item per source with query parameters derived from source.queryParams plus shared pagination params, and response schema envelope(array(recordSchema)); expose a registerRoute helper so later tasks (usage, keys, waitlist) self-register their own spec entries.
subtasks.details: Create src/routes/openapi.ts (or equivalent module per the chosen approach from subtask 1). Iterate the registry from src/sources at document-build time — never hardcode slugs — so adding a source file plus registry entry automatically produces its path item. For each source: derive query parameter schemas from source.queryParams zod shapes, append the shared pagination parameters, and set the 200 response schema to the success envelope wrapping an array of the source's recordSchema. Design a registerRoute(routeSpec) helper that appends arbitrary route definitions (method, path, request schemas, responses) into the same document, and use it to document /v1/health now; tasks for /v1/usage, /v1/keys, and /v1/waitlist will call it as those endpoints land. Set servers[0].url from an environment value with a placeholder domain until the real domain is purchased. tasks.title: D1 core schema, API key issuance, auth middleware, and revocation
tasks.description: Ship the account primitives: D1 migrations for api_keys/credit_ledger/stripe_customers, POST /v1/keys self-serve issuance (email in, key shown once, SHA-256 hash at rest), bearer-auth middleware with KV hot-path lookup of hash→key-record, and revocation support.
tasks.details:
1. `migrations/0002_accounts.sql`: `api_keys(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, key_hash TEXT UNIQUE, email TEXT, name TEXT, plan TEXT DEFAULT 'free', credits_granted INTEGER DEFAULT 250, created_at TEXT, revoked_at TEXT)`; `credit_ledger(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, key_id TEXT, delta INTEGER, reason TEXT, stripe_ref TEXT, created_at TEXT)` (append-only — no UPDATEs ever); `stripe_customers(stripe_customer_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, key_id TEXT, plan TEXT, status TEXT, updated_at TEXT)`.
2. src/auth/keys.ts: `generateKey()` → `fapi_<32 chars base62 from crypto.getRandomValues>`; `hashKey(key)` → hex SHA-256 via `crypto.subtle.digest`. `POST /v1/keys` (src/routes/keys.ts): body `{ email, name? }` validated by zod; insert api_keys row with free plan + initial `credit_ledger` grant (+250, reason 'free_tier'); return the raw key exactly once in the response with an explicit "store this now" message. Light per-IP rate limit on this endpoint (RATE KV) to stop key-farming.
3. src/auth/middleware.ts: extract `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; hash; lookup KV `key:<hash>` → key-record JSON (id, plan, revoked). On KV miss, fall back to D1 `SELECT ... WHERE key_hash = ?`, then populate KV (TTL ~1h). Missing/unknown/revoked key → 401 error envelope. Attach `keyCtx` to Hono context Variables for logging + metering. Apply to /v1/data/* and /v1/usage; leave /v1/health, /openapi.json, /v1/keys, /v1/waitlist public.
4. Revocation: `DELETE /v1/keys` (self, authed) and an `ADMIN_TOKEN`-guarded admin variant; set revoked_at in D1 AND delete/overwrite the KV entry so revocation is immediate despite the cache.
5. Add `.dev.vars.example` documenting `ADMIN_TOKEN` (secrets never in .env per CLAUDE.md).
tasks.testStrategy: Integration (pool-workers with real D1/KV bindings): POST /v1/keys returns a fapi_-prefixed key and the raw key never appears in D1 (assert only the hash is stored); authed request to /v1/data/:source succeeds; bad/missing key → 401 envelope; revoked key → 401 immediately (KV entry cleared); KV-miss path falls back to D1 and repopulates KV (spy via KV list). Unit: hashKey is deterministic hex; generateKey entropy/format.

subtasks.title: Implement src/auth/keys.ts crypto primitives: generateKey and hashKey
subtasks.description: Build the pure key-generation and hashing utilities using Workers-native crypto, with unit tests covering format and determinism. No routes or storage — just the primitives the issuance route and middleware will consume.
subtasks.details: In `src/auth/keys.ts` export (named exports, explicit return types per CLAUDE.md): `generateKey(): string` producing `fapi_` + 32 base62 chars ([0-9A-Za-z]) sourced from `crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(...))` — use rejection sampling or an unbiased mapping so the base62 distribution isn't skewed by modulo bias; and `hashKey(key: string): Promise<string>` returning lowercase hex SHA-256 via `crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', new TextEncoder().encode(key))`. Keep this module free of Hono/D1/KV imports so it stays unit-testable in isolation.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests (vitest Workers pool): generateKey output matches /^fapi_[0-9A-Za-z]{32}$/ across many iterations; consecutive calls differ; hashKey is deterministic (same input → same 64-char lowercase hex), differs for different inputs, and matches a known SHA-256 test vector.

subtasks.title: Build POST /v1/keys self-serve issuance route with free-tier ledger grant and per-IP rate limit
subtasks.description: Create the public key-issuance endpoint: zod-validated { email, name? } body, api_keys insert storing only the hash, initial +250 free_tier credit_ledger entry, the raw key returned exactly once with a store-it-now warning, and a per-IP rate limit on the RATE KV namespace to stop key-farming.
subtasks.details: In `src/routes/keys.ts`: zod schema `{ email: z.string().email(), name: z.string().optional() }` — invalid body → 400 in the task-1 error envelope. Handler: call generateKey(), hashKey(); insert api_keys row (id via crypto.randomUUID(), key_hash, email, name, plan 'free', credits_granted 250, created_at ISO) and a credit_ledger row (key_id, delta +250, reason 'free_tier') — use `env.DB.batch()` so key and grant land together. Response includes the raw key exactly once plus an explicit "store this now — it cannot be shown again" message; the raw key must never be logged or persisted. Per-IP rate limit using RATE KV keyed on CF-Connecting-IP with a short-window counter (e.g. 5 keys/hour/IP via TTL'd key) → 429 envelope when exceeded. Mount on the app as a public route (no auth middleware). This route stays niche-agnostic — no dataset-specific logic per the isolation rule.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration (pool-workers, SELF.fetch with real D1/KV): successful POST returns a fapi_-prefixed key and the warning message; querying D1 shows only the hash at rest (raw key appears nowhere); a matching +250 free_tier ledger row exists; invalid email → 400 envelope; repeated requests from one IP beyond the limit → 429.

subtasks.description: Build src/auth/middleware.ts: extract the bearer key, hash it, look up the key-record in KV with D1 fallback and KV repopulation (TTL ~1h), reject missing/unknown/revoked keys with the 401 envelope, attach keyCtx to Hono context Variables, and apply it to /v1/data/* and /v1/usage while health/openapi/keys/waitlist stay public.
subtasks.details: In `src/auth/middleware.ts`: parse `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; missing/malformed header → 401 envelope immediately. Hash via hashKey, then get KV `key:<hash>` from CACHE expecting key-record JSON `{ id, plan, revoked }`. On KV miss, fall back to D1 `SELECT id, plan, revoked_at FROM api_keys WHERE key_hash = ?`; if found, write the record back to KV with `expirationTtl: 3600`; if not found → 401. A record with revoked set (from either layer) → 401 with a distinct message but the same envelope shape. On success set `c.set('keyCtx', { id, plan })` and type it in the Hono Variables generic so metering (task 7) and logging consume it type-safely. Wire into src/index.ts so /v1/data/* and /v1/usage are guarded while /v1/health, /openapi.json, /v1/keys, and /v1/waitlist remain public.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration: freshly issued key → authed /v1/data/:source request succeeds; no/garbage/unknown key → 401 envelope; KV-miss path — delete the KV entry, request still succeeds via D1 fallback and the KV entry reappears with TTL; public routes respond without any Authorization header; keyCtx values surface correctly downstream (e.g. via a test route or log assertion).

subtasks.title: Add key revocation (self-serve + admin) with immediate KV invalidation, .dev.vars.example, and end-to-end integration tests
subtasks.description: Ship DELETE /v1/keys for authed self-revocation and an ADMIN_TOKEN-guarded admin variant, setting revoked_at in D1 AND deleting the KV entry so revocation bypasses the 1h cache; document ADMIN_TOKEN in .dev.vars.example and land the task-level integration suite (hash-only at rest, KV-miss fallback, immediate revocation).
subtasks.details: Self-serve: `DELETE /v1/keys` runs behind the auth middleware and revokes the caller's own key — `UPDATE api_keys SET revoked_at = ? WHERE id = ?` then `env.CACHE.delete('key:<hash>')` (recompute the hash from the presented bearer key) so the stale cached record cannot outlive revocation. Admin variant (e.g. `DELETE /v1/keys/:id` or admin route) guarded by comparing a bearer/header token against the `ADMIN_TOKEN` secret; it must also clear the KV entry, which requires reading key_hash from D1 by id. Order matters: update D1 first, then delete KV. Create `.dev.vars.example` documenting `ADMIN_TOKEN` (Worker runtime secrets live in .dev.vars locally / wrangler secret put in prod — never .env, never committed, per CLAUDE.md); ensure .dev.vars is gitignored. Then write the task-6 integration suite from the parent testStrategy.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration (pool-workers): issue key → authed request succeeds → DELETE /v1/keys → the very next request with the same key returns 401 (assert the KV entry is gone, proving cache invalidation not TTL expiry); revoked_at populated in D1; admin revocation works only with the correct ADMIN_TOKEN (wrong/missing → 401/403); full sweep asserting the raw key never appears in any D1 column; KV-miss → D1 fallback → repopulation regression test.

tasks.expansionPrompt: Split into: (1) migrations/0002_accounts.sql — api_keys (key_hash UNIQUE), append-only credit_ledger, stripe_customers — coordinating with the migration numbering/workflow established in task 3; (2) src/auth/keys.ts crypto primitives — generateKey (fapi_ prefix, base62 from crypto.getRandomValues) and hashKey (hex SHA-256 via crypto.subtle) with unit tests for format and determinism; (3) POST /v1/keys issuance route — zod-validated body, D1 insert + initial +250 free_tier ledger grant, raw key returned exactly once, per-IP rate limit on RATE KV against key-farming; (4) src/auth/middleware.ts — bearer extraction, hash, KV `key:<hash>` hot-path lookup with D1 fallback + KV repopulation (TTL ~1h), 401 envelope for missing/unknown/revoked, keyCtx attached to context Variables, applied to /v1/data/* while health/openapi/keys/waitlist stay public; (5) revocation — DELETE /v1/keys self-serve plus ADMIN_TOKEN-guarded variant, setting revoked_at AND clearing the KV entry so revocation is immediate, with .dev.vars.example documenting ADMIN_TOKEN, and the integration tests (hash-only at rest, KV-miss fallback path, immediate revocation).

tasks.title: Credit metering, free-tier quota, usage endpoint, and rate limiting
tasks.description: Meter every authenticated request: per-route credit costs debited against KV monthly counters, free tier of 250 req/month enforced, X-Credits-Remaining and upgrade-nudge headers, GET /v1/usage self-service endpoint, 80%/100% usage-alert thresholds, and best-effort per-key/per-IP rate limits.
tasks.details:
src/metering/:
1. costs.ts: `creditCost(route, source?)` — default 1 credit per data request (source.creditCost override), 0 for /v1/health, /v1/usage, /openapi.json.
2. counters.ts: KV key `usage:<keyId>:<yyyymm>` on CACHE; `incrementUsage(env, keyId, cost)` read-modify-write (accepted race: KV is eventually consistent, best-effort per PRD — document the Durable Objects upgrade path in a code comment + runbook, do NOT build it).
3. middleware.ts (runs after auth): compute balance = plan quota (`api_keys.credits_granted` + ledger top-ups cached in the KV key-record) − month usage. If exhausted → 402-style envelope (`code: "quota_exceeded"`, docs_url to pricing). Otherwise increment, then set headers on every metered response: `X-Credits-Remaining`, `X-Credits-Limit`, and at ≥80%/100% an `X-Upgrade-Nudge: <pricing docs url>` header + `meta.usage_alert: "80"|"100"` in the envelope (Dana's upgrade-nudge flow). Record threshold crossings in the request log.
4. `GET /v1/usage` (authed, free): `{ plan, period: "yyyymm", used, granted, remaining, alerts }` — reads counter + key record only.
5. ratelimit.ts on RATE KV: fixed-window per-key (e.g. 60 req/min) and per-IP for unauthenticated endpoints (keys issuance, waitlist); exceeding → 429 envelope with Retry-After. Best-effort by design.
6. Feed `creditsCharged` into the task-1 structured logger.
Keep plan quotas as data (constants module), not branching logic — pricing is launch-time config per PRD.
tasks.testStrategy: Integration: fresh key → /v1/usage shows 250 granted/0 used; N data requests decrement X-Credits-Remaining monotonically; header math matches /v1/usage; at 200/250 (80%) nudge header+meta appear; at 250 requests the 251st returns quota_exceeded envelope and no data; rate-limit test fires >60 requests in-window → 429 with Retry-After; counters roll over on month boundary (inject date). Unit: cost table, window arithmetic, balance calculation with ledger top-ups.

subtasks.title: Create src/metering/costs.ts: credit-cost data table and plan-quota config constants
subtasks.description: Implement `creditCost(route, source?)` as a data-driven lookup — default 1 credit per data request, per-source override via `source.creditCost`, and 0-cost entries for /v1/health, /v1/usage, and /openapi.json — plus plan quotas (free tier 250 req/month placeholder) exported as configuration constants rather than branching logic.
subtasks.details: Create src/metering/costs.ts. Export `creditCost(route: string, source?: DataSource): number` with explicit return type (per CLAUDE.md conventions). Structure it as a data table: a const map of zero-cost route paths (`/v1/health`, `/v1/usage`, `/openapi.json`) checked first, then `source?.creditCost ?? 1` for data requests. Add an optional `creditCost` field to the DataSource interface in src/sources/ if not already present (interface change only — no dataset-specific logic outside src/sources/<slug>.ts). In the same module (or a sibling plans.ts), export plan quota constants as data, e.g. `export const PLANS = { free: { monthlyCredits: 250 } } as const` — pricing is launch-time config per the PRD, so downstream code must read these constants, never hard-code 250 or branch on plan names.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests: creditCost returns 0 for each zero-cost route, 1 for an arbitrary /v1/data/* route with no override, and the override value when source.creditCost is set. Assert PLANS.free.monthlyCredits === 250 so a pricing change is a deliberate test update.

subtasks.title: Create src/metering/counters.ts: KV monthly usage counters with documented best-effort semantics
subtasks.description: Implement the KV monthly counter on the CACHE namespace under key `usage:<keyId>:<yyyymm>`: `incrementUsage(env, keyId, cost)` as read-modify-write plus a `getUsage(env, keyId, period)` reader, with the accepted eventual-consistency race documented in a code comment and the Durable Objects upgrade path noted in the comment and the runbook.
subtasks.details: Create src/metering/counters.ts. Export `currentPeriod(now?: Date): string` returning `yyyymm` (accept an injectable date so tests can exercise month rollover), `getUsage(env: Env, keyId: string, period: string): Promise<number>` reading the CACHE KV value (missing key → 0), and `incrementUsage(env: Env, keyId: string, cost: number, period?: string): Promise<number>` doing get → add → put and returning the new total. Zero-cost calls should short-circuit without a KV write. Add a prominent code comment: KV read-modify-write races under concurrency and KV is eventually consistent — this is accepted best-effort metering per the PRD; the strict-accuracy upgrade path is a Durable Object per key serializing increments (describe it, do NOT build it). Mirror that note in docs/RUNBOOK.md (create or append a 'Metering accuracy' section). Month rollover needs no cleanup logic — a new month simply starts a fresh key; optionally set a KV expirationTtl of ~60 days so stale counters self-expire.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests via vitest-pool-workers with the real KV binding: increment from empty key returns cost; repeated increments accumulate; getUsage on a missing key returns 0; currentPeriod formats correctly and an injected date in a different month yields a different key (rollover isolation). Verify the DO-upgrade comment exists (code review, not automated).

subtasks.title: Build the metering middleware: balance check, quota_exceeded envelope, credit headers, and upgrade nudges
subtasks.description: Create src/metering/middleware.ts running after auth: compute balance as plan quota (api_keys.credits_granted plus ledger top-ups cached in the KV key-record) minus month usage; return the 402-style `quota_exceeded` envelope when exhausted; otherwise debit and set X-Credits-Remaining / X-Credits-Limit on every metered response, adding X-Upgrade-Nudge and meta.usage_alert at the 80% and 100% thresholds and feeding creditsCharged into the structured logger.
subtasks.details: Create src/metering/middleware.ts as Hono middleware mounted after the task-6 auth middleware (which puts the key record on context). Flow: (a) `cost = creditCost(route, source)`; if 0, pass through but still set informational credit headers where cheap to do so; (b) `granted` = credits_granted + cached ledger top-ups from the KV key-record (do not query D1 on the hot path); (c) `used = getUsage(...)` for `currentPeriod()`; (d) if `used + cost > granted`, respond with the shared error envelope from task 1 — `code: "quota_exceeded"`, a docs_url pointing at the pricing page, HTTP 402 — and do not increment or serve data; (e) otherwise `incrementUsage`, then set `X-Credits-Remaining` (granted − new used, floored at 0) and `X-Credits-Limit: granted` on the response. Threshold logic: when new usage ≥ 80% or ≥ 100% of granted, add `X-Upgrade-Nudge: <pricing docs url>` and `meta.usage_alert: "80" | "100"` in the response envelope (Dana's upgrade-nudge flow); detect *crossings* (previous total below threshold, new total at/above) and record them in the task-1 structured request log. Always feed `creditsCharged` into the structured logger entry for the request. Keep all quota numbers sourced from the subtask-1 constants.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration via SELF.fetch with a seeded key: metered response carries both credit headers with correct arithmetic; exhausted key gets the 402 quota_exceeded envelope with docs_url and no data body; requests crossing 80% and 100% gain the nudge header and meta.usage_alert; log output (spy on console) includes creditsCharged and threshold-crossing entries; zero-cost routes never decrement the counter.

subtasks.title: Add authed GET /v1/usage self-service endpoint
subtasks.description: Implement GET /v1/usage (authenticated, zero credit cost) returning `{ plan, period: "yyyymm", used, granted, remaining, alerts }` in the standard success envelope, computed from the KV usage counter and the cached key record only — no D1 on the request path.
subtasks.details: Add the route in src/routes/ (e.g. src/routes/usage.ts registered in the /v1 group) behind the auth middleware but exempt from debiting — this falls out naturally because subtask 1 lists /v1/usage as a 0-cost route. Handler: read the key record from context (plan, credits_granted + cached top-ups), read the month counter via `getUsage(env, keyId, currentPeriod())`, and return `{ plan, period, used, granted, remaining: max(0, granted - used), alerts }` where `alerts` reflects thresholds already reached this period (e.g. ["80"] or ["80","100"]) derived from used/granted — consistent with the middleware's threshold math (share the threshold helper from src/metering/ rather than duplicating it). Define a zod schema for the response body so it flows into the OpenAPI 3.1 spec and MCP tool definitions per the single-source-of-truth convention. Response must be shaped so header math from subtask 3 and this endpoint always agree (same granted/used inputs, same helpers).
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration: fresh key → 200 with plan free, used 0, granted 250, remaining 250, empty alerts; after N metered requests, `used`/`remaining` match the last response's X-Credits-Remaining exactly; after crossing 80%, alerts includes "80"; unauthenticated request → 401 envelope; calling /v1/usage repeatedly never changes `used`.

subtasks.title: Implement ratelimit.ts on RATE KV and the full metering/quota/rate-limit integration test suite
subtasks.description: Create src/metering/ratelimit.ts: fixed-window best-effort limits on the RATE KV namespace — per-key (e.g. 60 req/min) for authenticated routes and per-IP for unauthenticated endpoints (key issuance, waitlist) — returning the 429 envelope with Retry-After; then write the end-to-end test suite covering monotonic header decrement, 80%/100% threshold crossings at 200/250, hard stop at request 251, month rollover via injected date, and >60 req/min → 429.
subtasks.details: src/metering/ratelimit.ts: `rateLimit({ scope, limit, windowSeconds })` Hono middleware factory. Window key `rl:<scope>:<id>:<windowStart>` on the RATE binding where id is the keyId (per-key) or client IP from CF-Connecting-IP (per-IP); get → increment → put with `expirationTtl: windowSeconds * 2`. On exceed: 429 with the shared error envelope (`code: "rate_limited"`) and a `Retry-After` header of seconds until window end. Comment that fixed-window + KV eventual consistency makes this best-effort by design (PRD-accepted; same DO upgrade path as counters). Mount per-key limiting after auth on /v1 data routes and per-IP limiting on the unauthenticated key-issuance and waitlist endpoints. Then the integration suite (vitest-pool-workers, SELF.fetch, seeded free-tier key with 250 credits): (1) X-Credits-Remaining decreases by exactly 1 per data request, monotonically, and matches GET /v1/usage after each batch; (2) request 200 (80%) is the first response carrying X-Upgrade-Nudge and meta.usage_alert "80"; request 250 carries "100"; (3) request 251 returns the quota_exceeded 402 envelope with no data and the counter stops advancing; (4) with an injected date rolled to the next month, the same key serves requests again from a fresh counter and /v1/usage shows the new period; (5) 61 requests inside one minute-window → 429 with Retry-After, and per-IP limiting fires on the unauthenticated endpoint.
subtasks.testStrategy: The integration suite described in details is the deliverable: quota arithmetic, header/endpoint consistency, threshold crossings at 200/250, hard stop at 251, month rollover via injected date, and both rate-limit scopes returning 429 + Retry-After. Unit-test the window-key derivation and Retry-After computation with fixed timestamps. All tests run under `npm test` with real KV bindings from the vitest Workers pool.

tasks.expansionPrompt: Split into: (1) src/metering/costs.ts — creditCost(route, source?) as a data table (source.creditCost override, 0-cost routes), keeping plan quotas as config constants not branching logic; (2) counters.ts — KV `usage:<keyId>:<yyyymm>` read-modify-write with the accepted eventual-consistency race documented in a code comment plus the Durable Objects upgrade path note; (3) metering middleware (after auth) — balance = granted + ledger top-ups − month usage, quota_exceeded 402 envelope when exhausted, X-Credits-Remaining/X-Credits-Limit on every metered response, 80%/100% X-Upgrade-Nudge header + meta.usage_alert, creditsCharged fed into the structured logger; (4) GET /v1/usage returning {plan, period, used, granted, remaining, alerts} from counter + key record; (5) ratelimit.ts fixed-window per-key and per-IP on RATE KV with 429 + Retry-After, applied to unauthenticated endpoints, plus the integration test suite (monotonic header decrement, threshold crossings at 200/250, hard stop at 251, month rollover via injected date, >60 req/min → 429).

tasks.title: Stripe billing: checkout sessions, idempotent webhooks to credit ledger, customer portal
tasks.description: Monetize the human channel with stripe-node on Workers: endpoint creating Checkout sessions for credit bundles (placeholder Starter $29 / Growth $99 / Scale $299), a signature-verified idempotent webhook handler mapping Stripe events to credit grants in D1 ledger + KV, a customer-portal link endpoint, and subscription lifecycle handling. Test mode only until launch.
tasks.details:
1. Add `stripe` dependency. src/billing/client.ts: `new Stripe(env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, { httpClient: Stripe.createFetchHttpClient(), apiVersion: <pin current> })`; webhook verification with `Stripe.createSubtleCryptoProvider()` and `stripe.webhooks.constructEventAsync` (SubtleCrypto — required on Workers).
2. Products/prices: write `docs/STRIPE-SETUP.md` + optional `scripts/stripe-setup.ts` (run manually, test mode) creating Starter/$29, Growth/$99, Scale/$299 monthly subscriptions with credit amounts in price metadata (`credits: 5000` etc.) — placeholder numbers are config, not code. Annual = 2 months free as additional prices.
3. `POST /v1/billing/checkout` (authed): body `{ plan }` → create Checkout session (mode subscription, `client_reference_id = keyId`, success/cancel URLs from env) → return session URL. `GET /v1/billing/portal` (authed): look up stripe_customers by keyId → `billingPortal.sessions.create` → return URL (Stripe-native dunning/cancel/upgrade — no code).
4. `POST /v1/billing/webhook` (public, signature-verified, raw body via `c.req.text()` before any parsing): handle `checkout.session.completed` (upsert stripe_customers, insert ledger grant `+credits` with `stripe_ref = event.id`, update api_keys.plan, refresh KV key-record), `invoice.paid` (recurring grant), `customer.subscription.updated/deleted` (plan change / downgrade to free). Idempotency: `INSERT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM credit_ledger WHERE stripe_ref = ?)` (or unique index on stripe_ref) so replays/retries never double-credit — the append-only ledger is the audit trail; always 2xx after recording to stop Stripe retries, log unhandled event types.
5. Metering (task 7) balance must include ledger grants — verify the KV key-record refresh propagates new credits promptly.
Secrets: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET via .dev.vars / wrangler secret (never .env). Live-mode object creation is an ask-first op per CLAUDE.md.
tasks.testStrategy: Integration with Stripe fixture payloads (recorded test-mode events, no live API): webhook with valid test signature (compute HMAC in test) credits the ledger exactly once; replaying the same event id changes nothing (idempotency); bad signature → 400 and no mutation; subscription.deleted downgrades plan and later requests reflect reduced quota; checkout endpoint returns a session URL (stripe client mocked via fetchMock). Manual test-mode end-to-end with `stripe listen --forward-to localhost:8787` documented in STRIPE-SETUP.md.

subtasks.description: Add the stripe npm package (ask-first per house rules on new top-level dependencies) and create src/billing/client.ts exposing a lazily-constructed Stripe client configured for the Workers runtime, plus an async webhook-verification helper using SubtleCrypto.

In src/billing/client.ts export `getStripe(env: CloudflareBindings): Stripe` that constructs `new Stripe(env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, { httpClient: Stripe.createFetchHttpClient(), apiVersion: '<pin the current stable version>' })` — the fetch HTTP client is mandatory because Workers has no Node http. subtasks.title: POST /v1/billing/checkout: create subscription-mode Checkout sessions
subtasks.description: Authenticated endpoint that takes a plan slug, resolves it to a Stripe price, and creates a subscription-mode Checkout session tagged with the caller's keyId, returning the session URL for redirect.
subtasks.details: In src/routes/ (wired through src/billing/): `POST /v1/billing/checkout` behind the existing auth middleware. Validate body with a zod schema `{ plan: z.enum([...plan slugs...]) }` (zod is the single schema source of truth — 400 error envelope on invalid input). Resolve plan → price ID via the mapping from subtask 2 (env/config, not hardcoded). Call `stripe.checkout.sessions.create({ mode: 'subscription', line_items: [{ price, quantity: 1 }], client_reference_id: keyId, success_url: env.CHECKOUT_SUCCESS_URL, cancel_url: env.CHECKOUT_CANCEL_URL })` — client_reference_id carries the keyId so the webhook can link the Stripe customer back to the API key. If a stripe_customers row already exists for this keyId, pass `customer` to reuse it. Return `{ url }` in the standard success envelope. Success/cancel URLs come from env vars (documented in STRIPE-SETUP.md), never hardcoded. Stripe API failures map to a 502-style error envelope with a request-id log line, no secret leakage.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration via SELF.fetch with fetchMock intercepting api.stripe.com: valid plan → 200 with the mocked session URL and the outgoing request asserted to contain mode=subscription, the right price ID, and client_reference_id=keyId; unknown plan → 400 zod envelope; missing/invalid API key → 401; Stripe 5xx mock → error envelope without stack or key material.

subtasks.title: GET /v1/billing/portal: customer-portal session link from stripe_customers lookup
subtasks.description: Authenticated endpoint that looks up the caller's Stripe customer in D1 and returns a Billing Portal session URL, delegating dunning, cancellation, and plan changes to Stripe-native UI with no custom code.
subtasks.details: `GET /v1/billing/portal` behind auth middleware. Query D1 `stripe_customers` by keyId; if no row exists (never purchased), return a 404 error envelope with a message pointing at /v1/billing/checkout and a docs_url. Otherwise call `stripe.billingPortal.sessions.create({ customer: stripeCustomerId, return_url: env.PORTAL_RETURN_URL })` and return `{ url }` in the success envelope. Portal configuration (which operations are allowed) is a Dashboard concern — reference it in STRIPE-SETUP.md rather than code. Keep the handler thin: lookup, one Stripe call, envelope; upgrade/downgrade/cancel flows generate webhook events handled by subtask 5, so no lifecycle logic belongs here.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration: seed a stripe_customers row in the test D1, fetchMock the billingPortal.sessions.create call → 200 with mocked URL and outgoing request asserted to carry the stored customer ID; key with no stripe_customers row → 404 envelope; unauthenticated → 401. Confirm the endpoint performs no writes to D1 or KV.

subtasks.title: POST /v1/billing/webhook: signature-verified idempotent handler mapping events to ledger grants and plan changes
subtasks.description: Public webhook endpoint that verifies the Stripe signature over the raw body before any parsing, maps checkout.session.completed / invoice.paid / customer.subscription.updated+deleted to credit-ledger grants and plan changes in D1, refreshes the KV key record, and is idempotent under Stripe's retry semantics.
subtasks.details: `POST /v1/billing/webhook` — public, no auth middleware. Read raw body via `c.req.text()` BEFORE any JSON parsing (parsing first breaks signature verification), then `verifyWebhookEvent(rawBody, stripeSignatureHeader, env.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET)` from subtask 1; failure → 400, zero mutations. Handlers: (a) `checkout.session.completed` — upsert stripe_customers (keyId from client_reference_id ↔ session.customer), insert credit_ledger grant of the plan's credits with `stripe_ref = event.id`, update api_keys.plan, refresh the KV key-record so metering (task 7) sees the new plan/credits promptly; (b) `invoice.paid` — recurring monthly grant via customer → keyId lookup, same idempotent insert; (c) `customer.subscription.updated` — sync api_keys.plan to the new price + refresh KV; (d) `customer.subscription.deleted` — downgrade to free tier + refresh KV. Idempotency: unique index on credit_ledger.stripe_ref (D1 migration) with `INSERT OR IGNORE` / `INSERT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM credit_ledger WHERE stripe_ref = ?)` so replays and retries never double-credit — the append-only ledger is the audit trail; never UPDATE balances directly. Always return 2xx once the event is recorded (including already-seen replays and unhandled types) so Stripe stops retrying; log unhandled event types with the request id. Verify with task 7's balance path that ledger grants + KV refresh surface in X-Credits-Remaining without waiting for cache expiry.
subtasks.testStrategy: Covered exhaustively by subtask 6's fixture suite (valid-signature crediting, replay no-op, bad signature → 400 no-mutation, lifecycle downgrade). tasks.description: Add The Gazette corporate insolvency notices as a DataSource — counterparty-risk/KYB bundle with uk-sanctions + sam-exclusions. Corporate slice is Blind-Mode viable via a structured-field WHITELIST: entry.title (= company name), category.@term (notice type, e.g. 'Petitions to Wind Up (Companies)'), f:notice-code (e.g. 2450), published date, geo:Point — ingest ONLY these; personal data exists at feed level (f:name/f:familyName) and insolvency-practitioner names live in the content HTML, so those fields are never read. Include notice-code range 2401-2599 (winding-up petitions/orders, liquidator/administrator appointments); exclude 2901+ (personal insolvency). Under the whitelist the task-38 per-dataset-terms question is moot — ships under standard OGL v3 Blind Mode posture, pending operator sign-off. Licence: OGL v3 Crown copyright, commercial reuse OK, personal-data exclusion noted in terms. Fair-use confirmed needed: 5 req/10s, identifiable User-Agent, bulk crawling 21:00-07:00 UK — existing 05:00 UTC cron (05:00 GMT / 06:00 BST) is inside the window year-round. WTP verified 2026-07-12: Endole GBP 25-39/mo (CH+Gazette bundle), Gazette own paid feed GBP 8,539/yr, Red Flag Alert GBP 2+VAT/search. Ranked #3 in docs/NICHE-RESEARCH-2026-07.md
tasks.details:
Implementation (spike de-risked the feed; no further probing needed before build):

1. Fetch layer — src/sources/uk-insolvency.ts implementing DataSource (src/sources/types.ts) + registry entry (src/sources/registry.ts). fetchFresh() pages GET https://www.thegazette.co.uk/insolvency/notice/data.json?noticetypes=<code>&results-page-size=N per included notice code (server-side filter via noticetypes param — no client-side code filtering needed). Include codes 2401-2599; exclude 2901+ (personal insolvency). Read f:total + pagination links; fetch newest-first and stop at the platform snapshot cap (~1000 records), like other sources.

2. Fair-use pacing inside fetchFresh: throttle to 5 req/10s (simple await-based pacing between page fetches), set identifiable User-Agent following the 'gankdat.com data refresh' convention. Cron stays 0 5 * * * (wrangler.jsonc) — 05:00 GMT winter / 06:00 BST summer, both inside the 21:00-07:00 UK bulk window; no contract change. Document the BST margin (06:00, one hour before window close) in the source-file header comment.

3. Blind-Mode whitelist normalization — recordSchema (zod) built ONLY from structured feed fields: company_name (entry.title), notice_type (category.@term), notice_code (f:notice-code), published date, and location from geo:Point if useful. NEVER read entry.content (free-text HTML carries insolvency-practitioner names) or f:name/f:familyName (petitioner/person names). Follow the data-minimization header-comment pattern established in src/sources/uk-sanctions.ts. Do NOT fetch per-notice JSON-LD detail pages — the list feed's structured fields are sufficient and detail fetches would multiply request volume against the fair-use budget.

4. Legal (was open question 2 in NICHE-RESEARCH-2026-07.md — now resolved pending sign-off): the whitelist keeps the corporate slice personal-data-free, so standard OGL Blind Mode posture applies; get operator sign-off on that call before launch. Still required before launch: terms.html licence-table row (OGL v3 Crown copyright, with the OGL personal-data exclusion noted and the whitelist posture stated). No privacy.html entry needed under Blind Mode. Same-commit rule applies to ARCHITECTURE.md 'Live datasets' + data-origins lines.

5. Fixtures + tests — record a real feed page into src/sources/fixtures/uk-insolvency.json (structured fields only); vitest unit tests for the feed→record mapping, plus a guard test asserting serialized records never contain f:name, f:familyName, practitioner names, or any content-HTML-derived text.

6. Exposure ritual per docs/NICHE-LAUNCH-CHECKLIST.md — stats spec (notices by month, by notice type; court only if a whitelisted structured field carries it — do not parse content for it), sitemap, registry-generated surfaces (/openapi.json, /llms.txt, MCP tools) verified, ARCHITECTURE.md updated same-commit.

All four candidate product shapes were examined and none clears:

DECISION: DEFER. No follow-up build task filed. tasks.title: D1-backed DataSource storage for large datasets
tasks.description: Platform capability (contract change, operator-approved 2026-07-13): a DataSource may declare storage:'d1' for datasets too large for the KV-snapshot pattern (KV 25MiB value cap + full JSON parse per request; breaks at ~168k records for sam-exclusions). Design: migration adds source_records(source_slug, generation, seq, search, record JSON, PK(source_slug,generation,seq)) + source_meta(source_slug PK, generation, last_refreshed_at, total). Refresh path in cache.ts: fetchFresh -> chunked batch INSERTs under generation+1 -> flip source_meta -> delete old generation (atomic swap, queries never see partial data; refresh_log unchanged). Query path: new src/sources/d1store.ts translates the EXISTING generic filter semantics to SQL — scalar string params as json_extract(...) LIKE '%v%' (case-insensitive substring), number _min/_max as numeric compares, date _after/_before as string compares (D1 sources must normalize dates to date-only ISO), q as LIKE over the precomputed lowercased search column, COUNT(*) total, LIMIT/OFFSET pagination. Constraint: D1 sources may declare scalar queryParams only (no array fields v1). Shared querySource(env, source, parsedQuery) dispatcher used by REST data route, MCP tools, and x402 lane; stats page uses SQL GROUP BY json_extract for D1 sources. subtasks.description: Extend refreshSource/refreshAllSources in src/sources/cache.ts so storage:'d1' sources ingest via chunked batch INSERTs under generation+1, precompute the lowercased search column, flip source_meta atomically, then delete the old generation — preserving refresh_log writes and the zero-records guard.
subtasks.details: In src/sources/cache.ts, branch on source.storage === 'd1': after fetchFresh (keeping the existing zero-records guard so a failed/empty upstream fetch never wipes live data), read the current generation from source_meta, then INSERT all records under generation+1 in chunks sized to respect D1's ~100 bound-params-per-statement limit (5 columns per row → ~19 rows per statement; group statements with env.DB.batch for per-chunk atomicity). Precompute the `search` column per record by lowercasing and joining the record's string field values (same corpus the in-memory q filter uses). Only after ALL inserts succeed, UPSERT source_meta(source_slug, generation+1, last_refreshed_at, total) — this single-row flip is the atomic swap point; queries key off source_meta.generation so they never see partial data. Finally DELETE the old generation's rows (best-effort cleanup; safe to re-run). On any insert failure, abort before the meta flip and delete orphaned generation+1 rows so the old generation stays live. Keep refresh_log writes and the existing KV path completely unchanged.

subtasks.title: SQL query engine: src/sources/d1store.ts translating applyQuery semantics to SQL
subtasks.description: New src/sources/d1store.ts that reproduces the exact generic filter semantics of applyQuery in src/sources/query.ts as parameterized SQL over source_records, including LIKE escaping, range compares, q full-text over the search column, COUNT(*) total, and LIMIT/OFFSET pagination.
subtasks.details: Build a WHERE clause scoped to `source_slug = ? AND generation = (SELECT generation FROM source_meta WHERE source_slug = ?)` so queries always read one complete generation. Translate each filter kind to match src/sources/query.ts behavior exactly: scalar string params → `LOWER(json_extract(record, '$.field')) LIKE '%' || ? || '%' ESCAPE '\'` with the user value lowercased in JS (SQLite LIKE is ASCII-only case-insensitive, so lowercase both sides in code) and `%`, `_`, `\` escaped in the bound value; `_min`/`_max` → numeric compares on `CAST(json_extract(record, '$.field') AS REAL)`; `_after`/`_before` → string compares on json_extract (correct because D1 sources normalize dates to date-only ISO — document this requirement where the module defines its contract); `q` → escaped LIKE over the precomputed `search` column with the needle lowercased. Run `SELECT COUNT(*)` with the same WHERE for total, and page with `LIMIT ? OFFSET ?` derived from page/per_page, ordered by seq for stable pagination. All values bound as parameters — never interpolated. Export a function shaped to slot into the dispatcher in subtask 4 (records + total).
